summary: Model updated for the read_only.go advance delete-key change (released ReadIndex requests are now freed); reference repaired for readOnly reset and forwarded-read handling. Fresh traces of the update revision validate. Model checking found and the real update revision reproduces a stale ReadIndex when a released context is reused and an earlier heartbeat acknowledgement completes the new request.
validation_limits: Update_full, Update_open, Update_discharge, inherited replication/ReadIndex/forwarded hunts and all simulations stopped at their time budgets (LIMITED_COVERAGE, not exhaustive).
The US4 stale-read counterexample was found only by a scenario-guided BFS (search-pruning CONSTRAINT over full MCSpec); unguided BFS/simulation within budget did not reach it.

Fresh traces do not observe higher-term reset with non-empty readOnly via vote/append/heartbeat, higher-term MsgReadIndexResp, BroadcastHeartbeat, ReadyAdvance, crash/restart or loss; these rely on model checking only.

Independent pre-existing abstractions not repaired: leader Progress reset in becomeLeader, append retransmission after rejection, lower-term append/heartbeat response branches, higher-term response step-down.
The specula CLI (findings registry, ci-result) and the controller confirmation workflow are not available in this environment; reproduction was performed in-run (spec/confirmation-MC-1.md).

findings.title: Reused ReadIndex context completed by a stale heartbeat acknowledgement yields a stale read index
findings.cause: read_only.go advance now deletes released requests, so addRequest admits the same caller context again in the same term, and recvAck attributes any in-flight MsgHeartbeatResp carrying that context to the new request.
findings.trigger: Release ReadIndex(C) while one follower's ack for that heartbeat round is delayed (or duplicated by MsgBeat); that follower helps elect a newer leader which commits; the old leader, still leader of its term, accepts ReadIndex(C) again; the delayed ack arrives.
findings.consequence: The old leader returns a ReadState whose index is below an entry committed before the request was issued, so a linearizable read served from it is stale.

premises: Callers may reuse a ReadIndex context after the earlier request with it completed.
Heartbeat acknowledgements can be delayed or duplicated.
The old leader has not stepped down when the stale acknowledgement arrives.
